meta.title: Recent housing roll calls and lame-duck funding outcomes
meta.purpose: Past votes the 2026 midterms brief uses to read how upcoming housing votes are likely to go. Each record names its public source and the date it was read.

roll_calls.measure: ROAD to Housing Act (H.R. 6644), final House vote
ROAD to Housing Act (H.R. 6644), Senate passage of the final version
HB24-1313, housing near transit, House passage
HB24-1313, housing near transit, final Senate passage

enactment_notes.note: The ROAD to Housing Act became law without the President's signature after he took no action within the ten-day window.
Full-year FY2026 HUD funding ($77.3 billion) passed the House 217-214 on February 3, 2026, ending a partial shutdown that began January 31.

SB25-313 (signed May 30, 2025) let the Division of Housing spend Prop 123 homelessness money on two state-owned supportive communities and put Prop 123 administration money under annual appropriation.

source.label: Legislative Council Staff, SB25-313 final fiscal note, August 6, 2025

enactment_notes.note: HB26-1360 moved $130 million from the state affordable housing fund (Prop 123) to the general fund on June 30, 2026, as part of the 2026 budget package.
SB23-213, the 2023 statewide land-use bill, died in the final hours of the 2023 session when the House and Senate versions were not reconciled.

lame_duck_funding.summary: Of 15 lame-duck sessions from the 103rd to the 118th Congress, regular appropriations were enacted during 5; work carried into the new Congress 9 times; interim continuing resolutions were enacted in 11.
